title: Fast Isotopy Computation for T-Curves
summary: A T-curve of degree $d$ is given by a regular unimodular triangulation of $d \cdot Δ_2$ together with a sign distribution on its lattice points. By Viro's Patchworking Theorem, this determines the ambient isotopy type (a.k.a. real scheme) of a smooth real plane projective algebraic curve of the same degree. We present a near-quadratic time algorithm for extracting that isotopy type from the triangulation and the signs. Through a GPU-accelerated implementation, this allows one to compute billions of real schemes per second, enabling exhaustive enumeration at scale. This algorithm was…
